record.paper_title: A collection of open problems in celebration of Imre Leader’s 60th birthday
record.original_question: If S is a subset of the integer lattice N^2 with the property that no three points of S lie on a common line, must the lower asymptotic density of S in [n]^2 vanish in the sense that lim inf_{n→∞} |S ∩ [n]^2| / n = 0?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 5.1. If S ⊆ N2 is such that no three points of S lie on a common line, then lim inf_{n→∞} |S ∩ [n]2| / n = 0.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{N}=\{1,2,3,\dots\}$ and for a positive integer $n$ let $[n]=\{1,2,\dots,n\}$. Call a subset $S\subseteq\mathbb{N}^2$ a no-three-in-line set if no three distinct points of $S$ are collinear (i.e., no three points of $S$ lie on a common line in $\mathbb{R}^2$).

Prove or disprove: for every no-three-in-line set $S\subseteq\mathbb{N}^2$,
$$\liminf_{n\to\infty}\frac{|S\cap[n]^2|}{n}=0.$$

Equivalently, show that no fixed infinite no-three-in-line subset of $\mathbb{N}^2$ can achieve $|S\cap[n]^2|=\Omega(n)$ along all sufficiently large $n$.
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture (an extensible / infinite version of the no-three-in-line problem, attributed to Erde) appears to remain open. Recent work by Nagy, Nagy, and Woodroofe on the extensible no-three-in-line problem provides constructions of fixed no-three-in-line sets in N^2 of size Ω(n/√log n) inside [n]^2, narrowing the gap to the trivial O(n) bound, and they conjecture the opposite (that Ω(n) is achievable). No proof or disproof of the lim inf = 0 conjecture is reported.

status_evidence.title: The extensible No-Three-In-Line problem
status_evidence.snippet: Constructions of fixed no-three-in-line sets in Z^2 with Ω(n/√log n) points in [n]^2; conjecture that Ω(n) is achievable, contrary to Erde's conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: Best known lower bound is Ω(n/√log n); conjecture remains unresolved.

status_evidence.title: A note on the extensible no-three-in-line problem
status_evidence.snippet: Erde's conjecture remains open. It contradicts more recent evidence by Nagy, Nagy, and Woodroofe who conjectured the opposite and provided computational support.
status_evidence.claim: Erde's conjecture (lim inf = 0) is described as still open.
